lead: >-
  On Wildlife and Safaris trips that include Uruguay, it is important to distinguish the countries on the itinerary from the actual wildlife-watching locations. On the current 32-day route, Uruguay's day is devoted to Montevideo, while an included marine excursion to see birds and sea lions takes place in the Galápagos Islands, Ecuador. If you are mainly interested in scenery and the coast, compare the separate nature tours that include Uruguay.
---

## Tours featuring Uruguay and wildlife watching: where is the relevant day?

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. **Uruguay appearing on the itinerary does not mean a safari or whale-watching excursion is included within the country.** The theme applies to the whole journey: one country may provide cities and culture, while another offers marine or forest wildlife.

Before choosing, identify the actual wildlife-watching day. If your goal is marine animals off Uruguay's coast, an itinerary with a city day in Montevideo does not meet that requirement. If you want a long journey across the continent with a separate island experience, the combination may suit you.

## Eight countries in 32 days: Montevideo and the Galápagos in different parts of the trip

[Eight South American Countries in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) combines Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia. It is a broad journey of cities, history, and natural areas, with wildlife watching forming a separate part of the long itinerary.

On day 9, travelers take a ferry from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). After a city tour and some free time, they return to Argentina. This day is about Uruguay's capital; it includes no separate marine wildlife excursion.

The observations that place this tour in the Wildlife and Safaris section take place later in the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Day 24 includes a marine excursion on one of two routes: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. The particular choice is confirmed after booking. These are alternatives, not two mandatory outings on the same day.

The itinerary describes colonies of birds, sea lions, and other island animals. Observation takes place **in Ecuador**, not Uruguay. Check the exact marine day and visiting conditions against the confirmed alternative; a sighting of any particular species cannot be guaranteed.

| Stage | Activities |
|---|---|
| Montevideo | Ferry, city tour, free time |
| Galápagos | Included marine outing to see island wildlife |
| Other countries | Cities, history, and landscapes according to the itinerary |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The overall duration is not the time spent watching animals. The 32 days include flights, road transfers, cities, and several natural regions. Compare this as an extensive journey with an island segment; if you want several days of dedicated observation in one location, look for a different format in the [general Wildlife and Safaris catalog](/interests/wildlife/tours/).

## Iguaçu, the Chaco, and Patagonia: nature alternatives

Other tours also include Uruguay, but they should not be recommended as programs with dedicated wildlife observations simply because national parks and waterfalls appear on the route.

The [16-day Uruguay and Paraguay tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) combines Uruguayan cities and the coast with the Chaco and Iguaçu. Visiting the Fortín Toledo conservation center and possibly seeing birds is not the same as an included independent safari. This itinerary suits travelers comparing scenery, culture, and a two-country journey.

The [13-day Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) combines Rio, Iguaçu, Buenos Aires, [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/), Montevideo, and a stay in [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/). The waterfalls are a natural attraction in their own right; the program does not include a separate wildlife-watching excursion.

The [Chile, Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay route](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) features Patagonia's mountains and glaciers, Iguaçu, and a city day in Montevideo. It is another landscape-focused alternative. These journeys can be compared under [nature tours featuring Uruguay](/interests/nature/tours/uruguay/).

## If you want wildlife on Uruguay's own coastline

This requires an itinerary explicitly providing local observation: a particular stretch of coast, time spent there, access arrangements, and guidance. An ordinary day in Montevideo and free time at a resort do not confirm these services.

First decide whether whales, seabirds, or other coastal wildlife interest you most. Then match the species' season with the location and included excursion. Seasonal animal presence does not guarantee sightings on a chosen day, while being able to see animals from shore is different from having an organized excursion included.

Explore the country's geography in our [Uruguay guide](/uruguay/) and available offers in the [Uruguay tours catalog](/uruguay/tour/). Discuss a private wildlife request separately from the conditions of already published journeys.

## How to compare an extensive journey with a specialist wildlife tour

For a long itinerary, count full days in your target environment, then time spent flying and changing hotels. One included island outing may be a worthwhile addition to the culture of eight countries, but it cannot replace several days with a naturalist.

Check which outings are included in the price, which are offered as optional extras, and which are alternative choices. For marine activities, boarding arrangements, time on the water, and possible weather-related changes matter. Compare scenic and cultural days separately: they are valuable in themselves but do not add time for observing animals.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is whale watching in Uruguay included?

The [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) reviewed here does not include a separate whale excursion in Uruguay. The Uruguayan stage is devoted to Montevideo, while the marine wildlife excursion takes place in the Galápagos.

### Why is a tour featuring Uruguay in the Wildlife and Safaris selection?

Because the full journey includes wildlife observations. They do not need to take place in every country on the route; check the location and day in the itinerary.

### Is Iguaçu a safari?

No. A standard waterfall excursion focuses on cascades and scenic trails. For that experience, explore [nature tours featuring Uruguay](/interests/nature/tours/uruguay/).

### Can I visit both Galápagos routes on the tour?

Day 24 includes one of two alternatives, confirmed after booking. Both are not advertised as included on the same day.

## How to choose a wildlife-watching tour in Venezuela

**On [New Conquistadors](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/), Los Llanos observations are scheduled for days 8–9; on [Beauty of Venezuela](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/), a safari is scheduled for day 11.** The second itinerary also includes a night safari around Maracaibo on day 8 and observation of dolphins and birds on day 9.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with included wildlife observation. Canaima's waterfalls, the trek to Roraima, and the Orinoco's river landscapes are covered separately among [Venezuela nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/venezuela/).

| Tour | Included observations |
|---|---|
| [New Conquistadors, 12 days](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/) | Land and water excursions in Los Llanos, days 8–9 |
| [Beauty of Venezuela, 12 days](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/) | Maracaibo, days 8–9; Los Llanos, day 11 |

A night safari on New Conquistadors is offered as an extra. The included daytime outings already provide a dedicated wildlife-watching program; particular species depend on conditions in nature. The country's geography is described in our [Venezuela guide](/venezuela/), and other destinations can be found in the [Wildlife and Safaris catalog](/interests/wildlife/).

## Los Llanos: two itineraries with genuine wildlife outings

The Los Llanos plains are one of Venezuela's most suitable regions for wildlife watching. Savannas, rivers, seasonal pools, and strips of riverside forest alternate here. Capybaras, spectacled caimans, herons, ibises, birds of prey, and anteaters live in the region. More elusive large predators also inhabit the ecosystem, but travelers should not expect to see a jaguar or puma on an ordinary tourist trip.

On the [12-day New Conquistadors tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/), days 8–9 take place in Los Llanos, Apure State. The itinerary includes staying at a ranch and traveling over land and water with local guides. A night safari is listed as **an additional possibility**, not an automatically included part of the trip. Before the savanna days, the route passes through [Choroní](/venezuela/place/choroni/) and [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) and then continues into the Andes.

Another option is the [12-day Beauty of Venezuela eco-itinerary](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/). Here, Los Llanos comes toward the end of the journey: after [Lake Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/), the Andes, and Barinas, days in the savanna include a safari. The description mentions birds, capybaras, iguanas, turtles, and possible encounters with other species. Unlike New Conquistadors, this tour also covers the Catatumbo and Lake Maracaibo region.

**The main difference is the surrounding geography of each wildlife segment.** The first tour spends more time on the Choroní coast and Andean highlands; the second adds natural areas of western Venezuela. In both cases, actual wildlife observations depend on water conditions, weather, and animal behavior. If your goal is bird photography, discuss early-morning departures and the length of waterside stops with the organizer before traveling.

Some Los Llanos programs may feature activities involving contact with wild animals. If you prefer observation and photography without catching or feeding animals, agree on that format separately.

## A scenic alternative: boat trips through the Orinoco Delta

The [Orinoco Delta](/venezuela/place/orinoco-delta/) is entirely different. Instead of open savannas, it consists of channels, swamp forests, mangrove areas, and islands. UNESCO describes the delta as a mosaic of river and coastal ecosystems with a wide diversity of birds, mammals, and aquatic species. For travelers, the primary experiences are travel by water, sounds of the tropical forest, and views along the banks.

On the [12-day Natural Contrasts of Venezuela itinerary](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/), **days 7–8 are devoted to the Orinoco Delta**. The program takes travelers to the Boca de Uracoa landing, followed by motorboat journeys through the channels. The description mentions birds, monkeys, and the possibility of seeing river dolphins with luck. These are potential sightings, not guaranteed encounters.

**The tour does not advertise a separate dedicated wildlife-watching activity.** Possible encounters on a boat passage complement the river scenery. This is different from Los Llanos trips: the nature segment is built around boat excursions in the lower reaches of a large river. Before the delta, the itinerary visits [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/) and [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), ending with relaxation on [Margarita Island](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/). It suits travelers seeking several ecosystems in one vacation, with the river section remaining a scenic journey with possible wildlife sightings.

For photography and observation in the delta, protect your luggage from water, bring binoculars, and be prepared for changing weather. The details of boat routes depend on water levels and local conditions. Meeting Warao communities, where included in a particular itinerary, is a cultural component of the trip rather than wildlife observation.

## Scenic alternatives: Canaima and Angel Falls

[Canaima National Park](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) is renowned for its tepui mountains, river valleys, and waterfalls. According to UNESCO, the park covers around 3 million hectares, and the tabletop mountains create isolated biogeographical environments. However, a tourist itinerary around the lagoon, waterfalls, and viewpoints primarily reveals **landscapes**, not specialist mammal tracking.

For a relatively short introduction, consider the [4-day Canaima and Angel Falls tour](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/). It includes [Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/place/canaima-lagoon/), [Sapo Falls](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/) and [Hacha Falls](/venezuela/place/hacha-falls/), a river expedition along the [Carrao](/venezuela/place/carrao-river/) and [Churún](/venezuela/place/churun-river/), and a walking section to a viewpoint of Angel Falls. The program provides several accommodation options, whose terms should be compared on the tour page.

The [6-day Colors of Venezuela itinerary](/venezuela/tour/colors-of-venezuela/) allows more time in Canaima after Caracas. Beyond the main waterfalls, it features free days and additional activities to choose from; flights, separate walks, and trekking should not be assumed to be included. For travelers seeking time for possible bad weather or a relaxed stay at the lagoon, this differs meaningfully from the shorter four-day itinerary.

Two other routes combine Canaima with the sea. The [12-day Popular Destinations of Venezuela tour](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/) continues from the capital and Canaima to [Margarita Island](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/). The [12-day Best of Venezuela tour](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) also includes Canaima, Angel Falls, and several beach days. **These are combined journeys with a strong nature component**, but without a dedicated Los Llanos safari or a boat-based Orinoco Delta segment.

For Angel Falls, season matters greatly: in rainy months, rivers are generally fuller, but cloud and heavy rain can restrict visibility and movement. In drier periods, shallow waterways can make the route to the falls more difficult. None of our programs eliminates the river excursion's dependence on current natural conditions.

## Scenic and hiking alternatives: Roraima

[Mount Roraima](/venezuela/place/mount-roraima/) suits travelers wanting to spend several days on trails, observe changes in vegetation, and reach the top of a tepui. This is a different pursuit from boating around Canaima or watching animals in Los Llanos. On the plateau, unusual rocks and plants can be seen, but the route is physically demanding and weather is changeable.

On the [12-day Mount Roraima trekking tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-mount-roraima-trek-12-days/), walking days and time on the mountain occupy a substantial part of the program, followed by Puerto Ordaz and Canaima. The [Active Venezuela: Jurassic Water World tour](/venezuela/tour/active-venezuela-jurassic-water-world/) also includes a multi-day hike up Roraima followed by Canaima's waterfalls. Both journeys belong to nature and adventure themes.

**Choose these programs for trekking and scenery**, not as a substitute for wildlife safaris. Before selecting, compare the number of walking days, overnight conditions, footwear and backpack requirements, organization of the treks, and participants' actual fitness. For other tours where traveling on foot is the main activity, visit our [Venezuela adventure tours catalog](/interests/adventure/tours/venezuela/).

## Nature plus Caribbean beaches or a second country

A nature holiday does not have to mean spending the entire trip in forests or on rivers. [Natural Contrasts of Venezuela](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) combines the delta, Canaima, Los Roques, and Margarita, while [Beauty of Venezuela](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/) connects Los Llanos with Choroní and western regions. A [Canaima and Margarita itinerary](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) leaves more time by the sea and covers fewer different natural areas.

There is also a [12-day Venezuela and Bolivia route](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/). Its Venezuelan segment features [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/) and Canaima, followed by Bolivia's [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), high-altitude lagoons, and volcanic scenery. Do not attribute Uyuni or flamingos in Bolivian lagoons to Venezuela: they belong to another country and another part of the journey.

If the sea is your main goal, explore the [Venezuela beach tours](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/venezuela/). If wildlife matters most, compare the number of observation outings rather than merely noting islands and national parks in tour titles.

## Seasons: why Los Llanos and Canaima require different decisions

Seasonality depends on the region. In Los Llanos during drier months, water bodies shrink, making it easier to observe birds, caimans, and other animals around remaining pools. During wetter periods, savannas flood and road and transport conditions change. In Canaima, higher water levels help river travel toward Angel Falls, although rain and clouds can interfere on a particular day.

| Area | Seasonal factors to check |
|---|---|
| Los Llanos | Water levels, roads, guided outings |
| Orinoco | Navigability of channels, weather, boats |
| Canaima | River flow and access to Angel Falls |
| Roraima | Rainfall, trail conditions, physical demands |

When combining natural regions, **there may be no perfect month for every goal**. Wanting to see as many savanna animals as possible while traveling by river to a full-flowing Angel Falls involves trade-offs. Before booking, establish whether the actual outings you are traveling for can operate, rather than asking only for a generic "best season in Venezuela."

## What to clarify before choosing a nature tour

**Can capybaras, jaguars, anacondas, or river dolphins be guaranteed?** No. A tour may include trips into their habitats, but the presence of a species in a region does not mean seeing it during a specific outing. The most predictable sightings often involve abundant or conspicuous species, while large predators remain rare encounters.

**Which itinerary is better for wildlife than for waterfalls?** Look for tours with days in [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/): [New Conquistadors](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/) and [Beauty of Venezuela](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/). For river scenery, a tour including the [Orinoco Delta](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) is a separate choice; it does not advertise dedicated birdwatching. The short Canaima itinerary focuses primarily on waterfalls.

**Is a nature tour suitable without serious physical preparation?** It depends on the itinerary. The long [Roraima trek](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-mount-roraima-trek-12-days/) demands considerably more than sightseeing walks in Canaima or boat trips. Yet even an Angel Falls river expedition can involve extended travel and wet trails. Compare the physical demands of each day.

**Are all listed excursions included in the price?** No. Some programs list night safaris, flights over Angel Falls, trips to additional lagoons, or island excursions as optional. Consult the "Included" and "Not Included" sections of the exact tour and the terms of the selected option.

**How should I prepare for wildlife observation?** Binoculars, a waterproof equipment case, footwear suitable for wet trails, rain protection, and insect repellent are useful. Do not approach or feed wild animals for photographs; follow local guides' instructions. Check current rules for visiting natural areas and possible transport changes before traveling.

The main selection criterion is simple: **count how many itinerary days are genuinely devoted to your nature interest**. All available routes, including those without a wildlife specialization, are listed in the [Venezuela tours catalog](/venezuela/tour/).

## Guadalupe Basilica, Mass, and the Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City

This excursion brings together two important aspects of Mexico: religious traditions at the [Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe](/mexico/place/basilica-of-guadalupe/) and the history of indigenous civilizations at the [National Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/place/national-museum-of-anthropology/). In a single day, travelers can visit a Christian pilgrimage site and a museum showcasing the diversity of Mesoamerican peoples.

We provide **a private excursion with an English-speaking guide and transportation**. The itinerary includes **one Holy Mass**, admission tickets to the listed attractions, and a subsequent museum visit.

## The basilicas and sacred Tepeyac Hill

The shrine on Tepeyac Hill is associated with devotion to Our Lady of Guadalupe, an important part of Mexican Catholicism. According to religious tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared to Juan Diego, and her image miraculously appeared on his cloak. For believers, this story underlies centuries of pilgrimage tradition.

The itinerary covers **the Old and New Basilicas**, Tepeyac Hill, the Chapel of the Indians, the Chapel of the Well, and the complex's gardens. Visitors learn about the original image of the Virgin Mary venerated at the shrine. The historic buildings have different architectural styles, while the new basilica is designed to accommodate large numbers of pilgrims.

**Mass is included in the itinerary.** Its timing follows the worship schedule, so it affects the sequence of chapel visits and the transfer to the museum. Modest attire is appropriate in religious spaces, and visitors should follow church rules during services.

## National Museum of Anthropology

After the shrine, the tour continues to Mexico City's National Museum of Anthropology. Its collections present the archaeological legacy of ancient cultures as well as material about the country's contemporary indigenous peoples. The museum provides historical context for Mexican traditions, which are encountered mainly from a religious perspective during the basilica tour.

The collections cover different eras and regions. A single excursion normally requires selecting galleries to visit rather than attempting to study every room. For this particular tour, **a specific list of exhibits** and the time allocated to each have not been defined.

This combination suits travelers who want to discover Mexico's Catholic heritage and its complex pre-Columbian history in one day.

## Included services and visit arrangements

The private excursion includes **an English-speaking guide, private transportation, admission tickets to the named sites, and one Mass**. The exact duration, price, and departure time for this excursion have not been specified. When booking, the visit must be coordinated with the Mass schedule, the museum's opening arrangements, and available transport routes.

The museum and shrine have different atmospheres: the former hosts educational tours, while prayer and worship are central to the latter. If anyone in your group finds prolonged walking or standing difficult, discuss arrangements for stops ahead of time.

For other cultural journeys through the country, explore [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about Guadalupe and the Museum of Anthropology

### Is Mass included?

Yes. Ada Tours' excursion explicitly includes **one Holy Mass** as part of the pilgrimage itinerary.

### Which basilicas and chapels are visited?

The program names the Old and New Basilicas, Tepeyac Hill, the Chapel of the Indians, the Chapel of the Well, and the shrine's gardens.

### Are transportation and tickets included?

Yes. **Private transportation and admission tickets** to the listed sites are confirmed.

### What language does the guide speak?

The description specifies **English**.

### Can I see the entire National Museum of Anthropology?

The extent of the museum visit depends on the agreed time. The published program does not promise every exhibition without exception.

## Tours featuring Mass at the Shrine of Guadalupe and the National Museum of Anthropology

The [Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe](/mexico/place/basilica-of-guadalupe/) in Mexico City features on pilgrimage and cultural itineraries. However, for travelers who particularly want to attend worship, it is important to distinguish an ordinary visit to the basilica from a program where **Holy Mass is explicitly included** in the excursion.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring the [Guadalupe Basilica, Mass and Museum of Anthropology excursion](/mexico/basilica-of-guadalupe/guadalupe-mass-anthropology/). It forms part of the [Religious Journey through Mexico: 7 Days](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/), scheduled for **April 1–7, 2027**. The visit to the shrine and museum falls on **April 2, day two** of the journey.

## What the Guadalupe day includes

After breakfast, the group heads to the Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe. During the excursion, you visit the Old and New Basilicas, Tepeyac Hill, the Chapels of the Indians and the Well, and the gardens, and learn about the revered image of Our Lady of Guadalupe. One Holy Mass takes place on the same day.

The next stop is the [National Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/place/national-museum-of-anthropology/), showcasing Mesoamerica's archaeological heritage and the cultures of contemporary Mexico's indigenous peoples. This combination provides two different experiences: participating in the shrine's religious life and exploring the country's history through museum collections.

This is a private excursion with an English-speaking guide. Confirmed included services are private transportation, guiding, admission tickets to the named sites, and one Holy Mass. For the services on other days, consult the tour's full itinerary.

In the evening, travelers return to Mexico City for dinner and an overnight stay at Casa Blanca 4* or a hotel of a similar standard. All six nights of the seven-day program are spent in the same hotel, allowing day trips without constantly changing accommodation.

## How this day relates to the five Masses

The pilgrimage lasts one week, with **Holy Masses on five days, April 2 through 6**. After the Guadalupe visit, the itinerary continues with different destinations:

- **April 3:** Mexico City's historic center, Mass at Santo Domingo, the cathedral, architectural monuments, and Garibaldi Square.
- **April 4:** the Shrine of San Miguel del Milagro, [Tlaxcala](/mexico/place/tlaxcala/), Ocotlán, and Puebla's churches, with another Mass.
- **April 5:** travel via Cuernavaca to Taxco, and Mass at the Church of Santa Prisca.
- **April 6:** [Teotihuacán](/mexico/place/teotihuacan/), Tulpetlac, and Tlatelolco, with Mass at the Church of St. James.

**April 1** is reserved for the airport welcome, transfer, and hotel check-in, while **April 7** covers breakfast and the return flight. Thus Guadalupe begins the main pilgrimage section without being its only component. The following days reveal different Christian shrines and historic cities of central Mexico.

## Who will enjoy this combination?

The itinerary is primarily for those whose important travel goals include attending Masses and visiting revered Catholic shrines. At the same time, it includes museums, archaeological sites, and colonial architecture. The [National Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/place/national-museum-of-anthropology/) visit, for example, adds broader historical context to a religious journey.

When planning, discuss time spent at the shrine, the order of visits to its different sections, worship schedules, and the pace of travel. If access to the churches and museum for a person with reduced mobility is important, assess the specific parts of the route.

Not every [cultural and historical tour through Mexico](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/mexico/) includes worship. Conversely, attending a single Mass does not mean a tour repeats the entire seven-day itinerary. Compare the actual days, places, and confirmed services.

## How to choose a tour featuring this excursion

When choosing, compare not just the number of shrines but also how the journey is organized. On the [seven-day religious tour](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/), accommodation is based in Mexico City, and most days involve returning to the same hotel. This differs from a long sightseeing route with overnight stays in several Mexican cities.

Check the trip dates as well: the published **April 1–7, 2027** dates apply specifically to this itinerary. On another route, visiting Guadalupe, attending Mass, time at the museum, duration, and dates must be confirmed separately. A basilica appearing on a tour's map does not in itself mean [this excursion](/mexico/basilica-of-guadalupe/guadalupe-mass-anthropology/) is included.

## Frequently asked questions about Guadalupe tours

### Is Holy Mass included at the Guadalupe Basilica?

Yes. The standalone excursion includes one Holy Mass. On the [seven-day tour](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/), it is scheduled for April 2, 2027.

### Is the Museum of Anthropology included on the same day?

Yes. After the shrine, the group visits the [National Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/place/national-museum-of-anthropology/). This is a separate cultural component of day two.

### Do we have to change hotels every day?

No. All six nights of this seven-day tour are spent in Mexico City at Casa Blanca 4* or a similar hotel. Day excursions also take travelers to other cities of central Mexico.

### Are there other Masses during the trip?

Yes. Five Holy Masses are included, taking place April 2–6. The full sequence is described on the [Religious Journey through Mexico](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/) page.

## Excursions to the Basilica of Guadalupe: pilgrimage and Mexico City history

The [Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe](/mexico/place/basilica-of-guadalupe/) is an active religious complex in Mexico City. It includes the old basilica, a modern circular church, chapels, and extensive grounds for pilgrims. An excursion here differs from visiting an ordinary historic monument: some people come to attend worship, and access to particular areas depends on the shrine's religious activities.

Ada Tours offers **two different excursions** featuring the shrine. One is intended for a pilgrimage with Mass; the other combines Guadalupe with the ancient city of Teotihuacán. Your choice depends on how much time you want to devote to spiritual tradition and how much to archaeology.

## Pilgrimage with Mass and a museum

[Guadalupe Basilica, Mass and Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/basilica-of-guadalupe/guadalupe-mass-anthropology/) is **a private excursion with an English-speaking guide**. Its route includes one Holy Mass and visits to the Old and New Basilicas, Tepeyac Hill, chapels, and gardens. Travelers then continue to the [National Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/place/national-museum-of-anthropology/).

Private transportation, an English-speaking guide, admission tickets to the named attractions, and one Mass are included. This itinerary suits travelers for whom worship is a substantial part of the journey. The museum adds a broader cultural context by introducing Mesoamerican civilizations and the country's contemporary peoples.

## Combining the shrine with Teotihuacán

[Teotihuacán and the Shrine of Guadalupe](/mexico/teotihuacan/teotihuacan-guadalupe-tour/) is **a 10-hour program** that combines the religious complex with the Avenue of the Dead and the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon at Teotihuacán. The excursion listing specifies English and Spanish, shared transportation, and a bilingual guide. Meals, drinks, tips, and personal expenses are excluded.

This program suits travelers who want to see monuments from different eras in one day: the religious tradition of modern Mexico City and an archaeological city that flourished long before the Aztecs. **A separate Mass is not advertised for this excursion.** Conditions from the other pilgrimage itinerary must not be applied to it.

## What to see at the shrine itself

The modern circular church opened in **1976** and houses the venerated image of Our Lady of Guadalupe. The Old Basilica retains architecture from an earlier period, while Tepeyac Hill and the chapels are associated with local religious history. Exploring the complex reveals both buildings and a living pilgrimage tradition.

Visitors can spend different amounts of time here: visit the main churches and image, linger in the square, or attend a service if included in the itinerary. Each chapel takes time to explore; a busy excursion that also visits Teotihuacán should not be mistaken for an in-depth tour of every part of the shrine.

## Mass times, clothing, and practical restrictions

The shrine's administration publishes worship schedules and conduct rules. When planning, check the specific date and access to the relevant churches. To attend Mass, agree on the service time and arrival rather than assuming worship begins whenever convenient.

Respectful attire is required in the churches according to the local dress code. The complex also includes open-air areas, so comfortable shoes, water, and sun protection are useful. During religious services, follow staff instructions on access and photography.

Other city and historical options are available in the [Mexico excursions catalog](/mexico/excursion/); themed routes can be compared under [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about Basilica of Guadalupe excursions

### Is Mass included in both excursions?

No. One Holy Mass is explicitly included in the [private pilgrimage program](/mexico/basilica-of-guadalupe/guadalupe-mass-anthropology/). The Teotihuacán itinerary does not list this service separately.

### Can I see the basilica and Teotihuacán in one day?

Yes. Ada Tours offers a combined excursion lasting **10 hours**.

### Which excursion includes the National Museum of Anthropology?

The museum is part of the itinerary with Mass. The Teotihuacán excursion has a different set of visits.

### Are there special dress rules?

Yes. The shrine has requirements for dress and respectful behavior. Check the complex's current rules before your visit.
